📨 Learning

Naive Bayes classifier

In simple words

A simple model that adds up clues, such as words, each counted separately, to guess a category like “spam”.

A simple, fast way to sort things into categories using probabilities. It counts how often each clue (for example, each word) appears in each category, then, for a new example, multiplies the evidence of all its clues together. It's “naive” because it treats every clue as independent and ignores their order. Spam filters used it for years.

Example. An email full of “free”, “win” and “click” piles up spam evidence word by word, while “homework” and “tomorrow” pull the other way.

Related words

  • ModelA program that has learned patterns from data and uses them to make predictions or create something new.
  • Supervised learningLearning from examples that come with the right answers (labels).
  • False positiveA false alarm: the model says “yes” (spam, sick, danger) when the true answer is “no”.
